boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Westport record (October 23, 1864) in Price's Missouri Expedition [September-October 1864]. Pleasonton's forcing of Byram's Ford the same morning is its own record (MO026); the pursuit to Little Santa Fe is context. Campaign-wide marches, recruiting, destruction, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Army of the Border and Army of Missouri; the live field reads zero. Price says the enemy engaged that day exceeded 20,000 well-armed men against his fewer than 8,000 armed, that a force of 2,000 or 2,500 threatened his train, and that he formed several thousand unarmed men and not more than 200 armed men to meet it. Britton says Curtis left three or four thousand militia in the Kansas City works and sent seven or eight thousand forward under Blunt, and that Shelby was reinforced by two of Fagan's brigades.
claims.rationale: Interested estimates and a history's figures for different scopes; no return at the battle. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory, and NPS says the Confederates could not break the Union lines and retreated. Price says Shelby and Fagan drove the enemy six or seven miles into Westport before he recalled them to protect the train; Britton says the Federal line first fell back behind Brush Creek, then the whole Confederate line retreated.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

open_questions: Curtis's (No. 64) and staff reports, Blunt's, Jennison's, Moonlight's, Blair's and Ford's reports, Deitzler's militia report, and Shelby's and Jackman's reports remain deferred.

Rosecrans's, Pleasonton's and Curtis's reports, the subordinate Union and Confederate reports in Volume XLI Part 1, the organization of Price's army (No. 89), Maclean's itinerary (No. 90), the Price Court of Inquiry, Hinton's 1865 Rebel Invasion of Missouri and Kansas, maps and returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page plus the frozen Arnold rows). Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam, 1899) is a retrospective history by a Union participant; by its preface the larger operations are based mainly on the published official reports, so it is not independent of the Price report family. Price's September 19 and November 2 dispatches and his December 28, 1864 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XLI, Part 1, No. 88) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
